JironFormBuilder.description: Jiron Form Builder's host configuration: the JironFormBuilder section of appsettings. It is for developers and for locks, and it wins over the backoffice. It is read once and checked when the site starts: a value out of range or a key Jiron Form Builder does not know stops the site with a message that names the key, and a change takes effect when the site restarts.

Root.description: The folder the default store keeps the files in: ~/ followed by a path relative to the site's content root, or an absolute path, for example a folder that the servers of a load-balanced site share (the default lies on each server's own disk, and a load-balanced site that keeps it is told so at start-up). It must not lie inside the web root or contain it, as written or with its links followed: a site configured so does not start. Name the folder by its own path, because the check cannot see through an administrative share, a drive letter made with subst, a short 8.3 name or a link inside the web root that points to the folder.

Limits.description: Hard limits that editors cannot exceed.

Definitions.description: How large a form may be. Each limit is at least 1 and at most ten times its default. A lowered limit refuses to save a form above it, and forms stored above it keep working.

MaxBytes.description: The largest document, in UTF-8 bytes: 2 MB.

MaxGroups.description: Groups per form, on all pages.

MaxFields.description: Fields per form, counting the fields of repeatable groups and the rows of grids, which store like fields.

MaxRules.description: Rules per form: those of pages, groups, fields, actions and outcomes, and the form-level validation rules.

Designer.description: Settings of field types and action types that the designer cannot change.

SettingLocks.description: Settings fixed for every form, for example the sender of every email action. Each names a kind, a type and a setting once.

items.description: A setting of a field type or an action type that is fixed in every form, for example { "kind": "action", "type": "email", "setting": "from", "value": "noreply@example.com", "hidden": true }. The designer shows it read-only, or not at all when hidden, a save that gives it another value is refused, and the site uses the locked value whatever a form says. The site does not start when a field type or its setting is missing, or the setting refuses the value.

Kind.description: Whether the lock is on a field type (field) or an action type (action), in any case.

Type.description: The type's alias, for example email: a letter, then letters, digits, '.', '-' and '_', at most 64 characters.

Setting.description: The setting's name at the top of the type's settings, for example from, spelt exactly as the type names it.

Value.description: The value every form uses, as text, at most 50,000 characters: a text, a number, a date, a time, a choice or a key as it is, true or false, a whole number as digits, a localised text as the text of every culture, and a list, an object or JSON written as JSON. Without one, the setting keeps its default.

Hidden.description: Hides the setting in the designer instead of showing it read-only.

Access.description: Who holds which permission: the global grants, set from the host.

Grants.description: The global grants, each naming a user group by its alias and the permissions it holds everywhere, for example { "group": "editor", "permissions": [ "viewEntries" ] }. With at least one, they replace the backoffice's global grants, which it then shows read-only; grants on folders and forms stay the backoffice's. Each group is listed once, and a permission comes with the one it needs (export with viewEntries).

items.description: A global grant from the host configuration.

Group.description: The user group's alias, for example editor. A group the site does not have is granted nothing.

Permissions.description: The permissions, in any case: design, manageActions, viewEntries, viewSensitive, editEntries, deleteEntries, export, manageLibrary, manageSettings, managePermissions or privacyTools.

Webhooks.description: The other hosts Jiron Form Builder may call: JSON option lists now, webhooks later.

AllowedHosts.description: The hosts that may be called, each a host name such as events.example.com or an IP address, in any case: no scheme, port, path or wildcard. None by default, so nothing is called.

AllowHttp.description: Whether http addresses may be called too; only https by default.

LockedSections.description: Backoffice settings sections that are read-only: general, email, protection, files, privacy, access (every grant and restriction) or integrations, in any case.
